name: brave--adblock-rust
instr:
# Port the Rust crate `brave--adblock-rust` to cpp (hidden tests)

You are given:
- `/app/rust_reference/` — the Rust crate's IMPLEMENTATION source (the spec).
- `/app/port/` — a cpp skeleton with the exact function/type signatures you must implement (unimplemented stub bodies).

Implement the skeleton so it FAITHFULLY reproduces the Rust behaviour. You are graded by a HIDDEN test suite (a translation of the crate's own tests) that you CANNOT see or run — reason from the source and implement exact behaviour (edge cases, errors, numeric precision, ordering).


## How to work
- Edit the existing implementation file(s) in `/app/port` in place. Declare each type, function and method exactly once: do not add files that re-declare skeleton symbols.
- Do NOT change the public signatures the skeleton declares — the hidden tests call them exactly.
- Implement it yourself; do not shell out to another program.
- The hidden tests use a header-only C++17 impl in `crate.hpp` plus a test file that `#include "test_harness.hpp"` and `#include "crate.hpp"`, with tests written as `TEST(Name){ CHECK(cond); CHECK_EQ(a,b); CHECK_NEAR(a,b,eps); }`. Do NOT write a main() — the harness provides it. Implement all signatures header-only in crate.hpp.

## Constraints (grading integrity)

Your `crate.hpp` is compiled with the test harness and EVERY `*_test.cpp` file into ONE program (`main.cpp *_test.cpp`, linked together); each test runs as its own process of that program and is graded solely by its PRO
